A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BVDV is able to invade neurons of the CNS of cattle.
BVDV infection of the brain of calves with MD and persistently infected cattle is a common finding, whereas the detection of BVDV in the CNS of calves with congenital lesions is rare.
in cattle persistently infected with BVDV, a widespread infection with BVDV is present in the CNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in cattle with BVDV-induced congenital brain malformation, BVDV antigents can only be demonstrated in neurons in very few cases.
the distribution of BVD virus antigens in the brain is different in persistently infected animals, in animals that have MD, and in animals that have congenital brain lesions.
the detection of BVDV in the brain of persistently infected cattle or of cattle with mucosal diseases does not prove a causal relationship between BVDV infection and congenital malformations.
